correctness.rationale: Irrational rotation with characteristic intercept supplies exactly n+1 factors and one unique left-special factor, the characteristic prefix z_n. For slopes strictly between 1/3 and 2/5, factor balance forces no 11,000,10101; every factor n>=6 contains at least two ones. A one-step tortoise image fixes the sum of two initial zero-run lengths and the trailing suffix. Only two distinct splits are possible, (0,2)/(1,1) and (1,2)/(2,1), and any collision suffix is left-special, thus one of the explicit characteristic prefixes. Distinct allowable left contexts produce both doubleton fibers, and initial zero-run lengths separate them. Full short-factor sets n<=5 yield the stated exceptional counts. Independently enumerated factors and compared all nontrivial fibers at n=1..23 for three irrational mechanical slopes (golden, sqrt(2)/4, (sqrt(2)+1)/7), all matching. Decimal enclosures and finite checks corroborate but do not prove the uniform irrational-rotation and left-special argument.

originality.rationale: Campbell–Rampersad (2026) introduced exactly the tortoise factor-complexity statistic, proved bounded loss under linear complexity/bounded gaps and a collision-to-left-special lemma, and computed exact formulas for non-Sturmian sequences. Their work explicitly raises Sturmian examples; it does not provide the two exact doubleton fibers and n-1 count for every irrational alpha in the full open interval. The original tortoise map and Sturmian n+1 factor theorem are classical inputs. A later/unindexed exact Fibonacci/Sturmian computation could overlap.
